name: Ugaritic Baal Cycle

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: The Baal Cycle survives on Late Bronze Age cuneiform tablets excavated at Ugarit/Ras Shamra.

earliest_written_attestation.note: KTU 1.1–1.6 belong to the Ugaritic Late Bronze Age textual corpus.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The surviving cuneiform tablets themselves provide the manuscript horizon.

tradition_internal_claim.note: The cycle narrates divine conflicts and kingship rather than historical calendar events.

dating.dating_summary: The Baal Cycle is securely preserved in the Late Bronze Age Ugaritic archive; this seed does not assign a point date to first composition or an earlier oral form.

notes: Added for Phase 7 because scholarship explicitly discusses Yahwistic appropriation/adaptation of Baalistic storm and combat imagery. The narrative node itself does not assert that influence.
